name: Impersonator
flavor: The discipline of the mimic: a Doppelganger who spends less time studying combat forms and more time studying people — their faces, their voices, their little tells — until borrowing a life, or a single trick from one, is second nature.

features.name: Perfect Mimicry
features.description: You have practiced copying more than a silhouette. As an action, you can assume the exact physical appearance — clothing, minor scars, voice, and posture included — of any Medium or Small humanoid you have observed for at least 1 minute, for up to 1 hour or until you end it early (no action required) or use this feature again. This changes only your outward appearance, not your game statistics, and any equipment you're wearing or carrying isn't transformed along with you. While disguised this way, you have advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks made to pass yourself off as that specific individual, and a creature without a particular reason to be suspicious can't tell you're a fake without succeeding on a Wisdom (Insight) check contested by your Deception check (or other means, such as true seeing). There is no limit on how often you do this — you hold **one** face at a time, and taking a new one ends the old.
features.narration: You put on a face like a coat. Not a disguise — the scar, the voice, the way they stand when they are bored, all of it, down to the habits they do not know they have. People who have known them for years walk straight past you.

meta.uses: At will, one at a time

features.sheetSummary: Action, at will, 1 hour, one face at a time. Assume the exact appearance and voice of a Medium or Small humanoid you observed for 1+ minute. Appearance only — statistics and gear are unchanged. Advantage on Deception to pass as them; seeing through it takes an Insight check vs your Deception.

features.name: Borrowed Trick
features.description:
You do not copy what a blow was made of — you copy the thing that made it. When a creature you can see within 30 feet makes an attack, hit or miss, you memorise that attack. You hold one at a time; memorising a new one replaces it, and it fades when the fight ends.

**Once per combat, the next Clone you create comes out as a Mimic** — it wears that creature's face and build instead of yours. In every other respect it is an ordinary Clone: it counts against your cap, obeys your leash, and can be used by Swap, Mirror Image, Decoy Detonation and the rest.
features.narration: You watch it swing once and that is all you need. The next reflection you leave behind is not wearing your face — it is wearing theirs, standing where you put it, holding the same weapon at the same angle. The look on the original's face is the entire reason you learned this.
features.sheetSummary: Memorise an attack made by a creature you can see within 30 ft (hit or miss); you hold one at a time. Once per combat, your next Clone spawns as a Mimic of that creature. What it copies and its limits are listed below.

meta.action: Free to memorise · Bonus Action to create

options.name: Its face and build
options.effect: The Clone looks like the memorised creature rather than like you.

options.name: Its Armour Class
options.effect: The Mimic uses the copied creature's AC instead of yours — which can be better or worse than your own.

options.name: That one attack, and nothing else
options.effect: Whenever the Mimic attacks — through Mirror Barrage, Mirror Assault, or any feature that has a Clone strike — it makes the memorised attack, using the copied creature's attack bonus and damage, instead of your weapon and Constitution. It has no other action, trait or ability of that creature.

options.name: Nothing bigger than you
options.effect: You can only mimic a creature of your own size or smaller. A Medium Doppelganger can copy a Small or Medium creature and can never copy a Large or Huge one.

options.name: It is still made of glass
options.effect: A Mimic has no hit points. The first attack that hits it destroys it, exactly like any other Clone, however good the AC it borrowed.

options.name: Half damage still applies
options.effect: Mirror Barrage halves a Clone's damage as normal, including a Mimic's borrowed attack.

features.name: Treacherous Opening
features.description: A borrowed face is a weapon the moment you stop needing it. Once per combat, the first attack roll you make against a creature that currently believes a Perfect Mimicry disguise of yours is genuine is made with advantage and deals an extra [[1d6]] damage on a hit. Making an attack immediately ends the deception for every creature that sees it — the face stays, but nobody believes it anymore.
features.narration: They are still talking to a face they trust when it hits them. That is the whole trick, and it only works once per face, because after that nobody in the room believes anything wearing it.
features.sheetSummary: 1/combat. Your first attack roll against a creature currently fooled by your Perfect Mimicry has advantage and deals an extra [[1d6]] damage on a hit. Attacking ends the deception for every creature that sees it.
